title: Sasol partners with DSTI, SANEDI and North-West University to build local hydrogen technology capability
summary: Sasolburg, South Africa – Sasol, the Department of Science, Technology and Innovation, the South African National Energy Development Institute and North-West University have commissioned a 2kW Proton Exchange Membrane electrolyser at Sasol’s Research and Technology campus in Sasolburg, marking a meaningful step forward in South Africa’s drive to build local hydrogen technology capability.
body_markdown:
# Overview


Through proprietary technologies and processes the main products Sasol produces are fuel components, chemical components and co-products. From these main products and further value-adding processes we deliver diesel, petrol (gasoline), naphtha, kerosene (jet fuel), liquid petroleum gas (LPG), olefins, alcohols, polymers, solvents, surfactants, co-monomers, ammonia, methanol, crude tar acids, sulphur, illuminating paraffin, bitumen and fuel oil. Even further processing produces numerous additional products.
